instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.text: North America and Europe move about 2.5 centimetres further apart every year! That’s about the speed that your fingernails grow!
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.text: About 4.6 billion years ago, the Earth’s crust broke apart into tectonic plates of various sizes.
Today, there are seven large plates and over fifty smaller plates. Although they are tightly packed, they are constantly moving at a very slow rate.
There are two different types of tectonic plate. Oceanic plates are found mostly under the sea, and continental plates are mostly under land.

atoms.a: What are the different pieces of the Earth’s crust called?
How many large tectonic plates are there?

b: ++a tectonic plate that is mostly under the sea
a tectonic plate that sits mostly under land
a tectonic plate that can be found in the inner core

feedback.end: These tectonic plates are around 62 miles thick! The largest of the plates is the Pacific Plate, and the smallest is the South American Plate.
